dedupe_keys.name: lazard levelized cost of energy lcoe annual report

description: Lazard's Levelized Cost of Energy+ (LCOE+) is an annual report that compares the cost competitiveness of new-build and existing generation technologies and of energy storage, produced by the financial advisory firm Lazard since 2007 and now extended with system-level considerations such as firming, reliability and replacement capacity. The 2026 edition, available as a 1.1 MB PDF from the landing page, analyses the cost competitiveness of renewables, energy storage and system considerations, finds renewables the most cost-competitive new-build generation on an unsubsidised basis and notes that storage costs rose, reversing recent declines. Coverage is mainly the United States, with some global comparisons; the values are ranges for representative plants, not asset-level data. Access: a direct PDF download from the page with no registration shown. Licence and cost: free to read; the page states no reuse licence, so the tables cannot be assumed open. Caveats: assumptions on capital cost, fuel price, capacity factor and cost of capital drive the results, the cost tables are printed in the PDF only, and Lazard is a commercial adviser, not a regulator. It suits capacity planning and investment appraisal inputs for infrastructure simulation, alongside official EIA statistics catalogued here.
